question: Action against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing: EU-guidance on implementation of Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008

Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/20081 requires Member States to take appropriate action against nationals who support or engage in illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing. Articles 39(2) and 40(1) are particularly relevant to preventing IUU fishing and ensuring that EU-based operators and beneficial owners cannot evade their responsibilities under EU law by operating vessels under third-country flags.

However, implementation has been uneven across the EU. Member States have identified the need for practical guidance on how to identify, collect and exchange information concerning the interests of EU nationals, including ultimate beneficial owners, in fishing vessels flying the flag of third countries. The Commission has established the Working Group on Nationals to support the implementation of these provisions.
However, the group has reportedly only met once since its creation in 2024. 1.

What measures is the Commission currently taking to improve implementation and enable competent authorities to identify and collect information on EU nationals’ legal, beneficial or financial interests in, or control over, foreign-flagged fishing vessels?

When will the Commission publish a formal, practical guidance document to assist Member States on how to identify, collect and exchange information on EU nationals’ interests in foreign-flagged fishing vessels?
Will the Commission reconvene the Working Group on Nationals on a regular basis?

Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 of 29 September 2008 establishing a Community system to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2008/1005/oj).
